title: Striking the Benefit on a Rider Line According to its Benefit Category
content:
The way the benefit on a line under one of the Optional Supplemental Benefit Riders is struck follows from the benefit category the line falls in.

## The rule

**Where the line's benefit category carries a flat allowance**, the benefit is the lesser of what is carried into the benefit calculation and that flat allowance, and no percentage is taken.

**Where the line is a hearing examination**, the benefit is what is carried into the benefit calculation less the hearing examination copayment the rider held carries.

**Otherwise**, the benefit year's deductible is taken off first where it is due, the coinsurance percentage the line's benefit category carries is taken on what is left, and the result is rounded to the nearest cent.

## When the deductible is due

The deductible is due where the line falls in one of the benefit categories the rider takes its deductible on — basic restorative dental care, major restorative dental care, root canal treatment, gum treatment, oral surgery, dentures and implants — and the rider has paid no line in any such category in the benefit year. Where a line in any of those categories has already been paid in the benefit year, no deductible is due on this line. Preventive care is never subject to a deductible.

## Input, judgement, output

| Input | Judgement | Output |
|---|---|---|
| A line for eyeglass frames, 300.00 USD carried into the calculation, the rider's frame allowance being 175.00 USD | The category carries a flat allowance | The lesser of the two, 175.00 USD; no percentage is taken |
| A line for eyeglass frames, 120.00 USD carried into the calculation, the rider's frame allowance being 175.00 USD | The category carries a flat allowance | The lesser of the two, 120.00 USD |
| A hearing examination, 90.00 USD carried into the calculation, the rider's hearing examination copayment being 0.00 USD | The line is a hearing examination | 90.00 USD, being what is carried in less that copayment |
| A root canal, 800.00 USD carried in, deductible of 75.00 USD due, the root canal share being 60 per cent | Neither a flat allowance nor a hearing examination | The deductible leaves 725.00 USD, and 60 per cent of that is 435.00 USD |
| A second root canal in the same benefit year, 800.00 USD carried in, a line in a deductible category already paid, the share being 60 per cent | No deductible is due | 60 per cent of 800.00 USD, that is 480.00 USD |

Every figure in the table above is a hypothetical input.

## Note on order

Where the third case governs, the deductible comes off before the percentage is taken, never after it; and the rounding to the nearest cent is done on the result, once the percentage has been taken.
